title: Siegard plan node
description: One node of a development plan: the frontmatter of one markdown file under the work root. The path is the identity — `inventory/<slug>.md`, `epic/<slug>.md`, `task/<epic>/<slug>.md` — so no id, type or epic field exists to disagree with it. `kind` is supplied by the validator from the path and is never written in a file; the examples omit it the same way. A plan node deliberately carries no status, estimate, priority or order field: execution state lives in git, and order is derived from dependencies by whoever executes — a plan that records progress is an orchestrator's state file, which this framework refuses to have. A task names the specification nodes it implements by identity, and nothing more: the specification does not change during a plan's execution, by convention, so there is nothing here to pin against staleness. One example per kind sits in that kind's branch. The body below the frontmatter carries exactly two headings, `## What it is` and `## Notes`.

kind.description: Supplied by the validator from the file path; never written in frontmatter.

summary.description: One sentence saying what the node holds, not what kind it is.

rationale.description: Why the planning decided this. Present means the planning decided; absent means the scope or the specification stated it.

sources.description: Where this node was read from — ordinarily files under the work root's `intake/`, which the validator never reads.

area.description: The paths the survey walked, as the caller named the target source root — the root itself when the survey walked all of it. Required even when the target is empty: a greenfield area is a full answer, said in `summary`, and this field still records where the survey looked.

modules.description: What already exists where the change lands. Absent when the area holds nothing.

conventions.description: How the existing code does things, each with the path it was seen at. A convention without evidence is an opinion, and opinions are not inventory.

must_not_duplicate.description: What the plan's tasks must reuse rather than rewrite, each with where it sits.

risks.description: What the change could break, each with the consumers that would observe it. A risk with no named consumer is a worry, not a risk.

covers.description: The specification nodes this epic answers for, in both directions: the validator requires every entry to be implemented by one of the epic's tasks or declared in `uncovered` — a covered node reaches a task or a stated why, never neither — and refuses a task naming a node outside this list in `implements`, because a reference outside the claim is scope the plan does not declare. Two epics may cover the same specification node — overlap is shared scope declared, never an error — and each reconciles its own claim independently.

uncovered.description: The deliberate remainder of `covers`: specification nodes this epic claims and this plan leaves untouched, each with why. An entry here that a task nevertheless implements is a contradiction the validator refuses.

objective.description: The one falsifiable outcome this task delivers. Two outcomes are two tasks.

criteria.description: The conditions under which the objective counts as met, each falsifiable on its own. "Works correctly" is prose; "a rejected order returns the stated domain error" is a criterion.

depends_on.description: Tasks whose delivered outcome this one builds on. Dependency, never order: the validator refuses a cycle, and any schedule satisfying these edges is equally valid.

produces.description: The artifacts this task's delivery must create, by path relative to the target source root. It is the checkable half of an objective rather than a second statement of it, and it exists because two things read it. A delivery refuses an implementation record whose `files` does not list what the task said it would produce, so the claim is held to what was written rather than to what was meant. And a task producing anything is one building what the project's own standard presupposes — the manifest, the compiler configuration, the artifact a rule names and no rule can ask for — which is why writing source over an absent presupposition stops for every other task and never for this one: holding the task that builds the substrate to the substrate's presence is circular, and the deadlock has no other exit. Ordinary work declares none.
produces.$comment: Held against the implementation record's `files` by bin/deliver.py, and read by /implement-task before anything is written.

implements.description: The specification nodes this task implements, by identity: the executor reads exactly these, current, from the specification itself — the specification does not change during a plan's execution, by convention, so there is nothing to pin. Every entry sits inside the epic's `covers`; a task needing more grows the claim or moves. A task implementing none is ungoverned by the specification and must say why in `rationale`.

examples.title: Order service
examples.summary: The area the checkout scope lands in: one layered service under src/.

conventions.statement: Route handlers stay thin and delegate to a service module.

risks.risk: The billing client is shared; a signature change ripples.

examples.title: Checkout
examples.summary: Everything order placement needs, from recording to refusal.

uncovered.why: State handling ships with the follow-up scope; nothing in this plan transitions an order.

examples.title: Record a placed order
examples.summary: The entry point that persists a valid order.
examples.objective: A valid order submitted to the service is persisted and retrievable by its order_number.
criteria: Submitting a valid order returns its order_number.
An order with a non-positive total is refused with the stated rule.

slug.description: A name reduced to kebab-case. A name that will not reduce is a refusal, not a transliteration.

specNodeRef.description: A specification node, by identity (SPEC-003 R1): its path from the specification root, without `.md`.

taskRef.description: A task of this plan, by identifier.

role.description: Whether the change lands in it, leans on it, or merely sits next to it.

seen_at.description: The path the convention was observed at.
